newsitem.title: ITALY: Deroma makes good debut, pleases analysts.
newsitem.headline: Deroma makes good debut, pleases analysts.

text.p: Analysts were positive for the future of terracotta pot maker Deroma Holding which made its debut on the Milan bourse on Monday.
"Deroma is the world leader in the sector with a 25 percent market share," said Marco Opipari of Intersim brokers. "It's in a very strong competitive position."
The Vicenza-based group started trading at a session high of 11,950 lire against a share flotation price of 10,000 lire.
Opipari said that after looking at 1997 profit estimates for Deroma and its nearest competitor ceramics group Pagnossin the share value would be around 13,000 lire.

He noted Deroma had high rates of turnover growth and good profit margins. The company had estimated 1996 turnover of 114 billion lire, against 107 billion in 1995, with some 80 percent coming from sales abroad.
Federico Milla of Milla Sim said the company had marked out "an interesting strategy."
"The sector can show good margins if production can be carried out on the spot due to high transport costs," he said noting Deroma planned acquisitions in the U.S.
The company, established in 1955, has several manufacturing centres including ones in China and Denmark.
At 1450 GMT, Deroma was quoted at 11,500 lire in volume of 997,000 shares.
